headline: ICT-2 to deliver verdict in case against Obaidul Quader and 6 others today
summary: The tribunal will rule on charges of crimes against humanity related to the 2024 July uprising, with all seven accused currently absconding.
details: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 is set to deliver its verdict today in a crimes against humanity case against Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader and six others.
The case concerns atrocities committed during the July uprising in 2024, with the prosecution alleging that more than 1,400 protesters were killed and over 25,000 seriously injured.
According to the prosecution, Quader used his position as AL general secretary and cabinet minister to control law enforcement and armed cadres to violently suppress the quota reform movement.
Other accused include former state minister Mohammad Ali Arafat, AL Joint General Secretary AFM Bahauddin Nasim, and Jubo League leaders Sheikh Fazle Shams Parash and Moinul Hossain Nikhil.
The charges also involve Chhatra League leaders Saddam Hussain and Sheikh Wali Asif Enan, who are accused of coordinating attacks and assembling armed cadres.
The trial began on February 17, following an investigation that started in June 2025 and the framing of charges in January 2026.
After eight months of trial and testimony from 29 prosecution witnesses, the tribunal announced yesterday that the verdict would be delivered today.
All seven accused individuals are currently absconding.

The International Crimes Tribunal-2 is set to deliver its verdict today in a crimes against humanity case against Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader and six others.

The case concerns atrocities committed during the July uprising in 2024, with the prosecution alleging that more than 1,400 protesters were killed and over 25,000 seriously injured.

According to the prosecution, Quader used his position as AL general secretary and cabinet minister to control law enforcement and armed cadres to violently suppress the quota reform movement.

Other accused include former state minister Mohammad Ali Arafat, AL Joint General Secretary AFM Bahauddin Nasim, and Jubo League leaders Sheikh Fazle Shams Parash and Moinul Hossain Nikhil.

The charges also involve Chhatra League leaders Saddam Hussain and Sheikh Wali Asif Enan, who are accused of coordinating attacks and assembling armed cadres.

The trial began on February 17, following an investigation that started in June 2025 and the framing of charges in January 2026.

After eight months of trial and testimony from 29 prosecution witnesses, the tribunal announced yesterday that the verdict would be delivered today.

All seven accused individuals are currently absconding.

headline_marked: Mymensingh hospital fire: [[Reports of 6 stampede deaths incorrect]], says commissioner
headline: Mymensingh hospital fire: Reports of 6 stampede deaths incorrect, says commissioner
summary: Divisional Commissioner SM Humayun Kabir Sarkar clarified that no one died in a stampede following a blaze at Mymensingh Medical College Hospital.
details: A fire broke out at Mymensingh Medical College Hospital (MMCH) around 6:00 pm on Monday, causing smoke to spread across multiple floors and triggering widespread panic among patients and attendants.
Fire Service officials deployed 10 units from five stations to the scene, bringing the blaze under control by approximately 6:30 pm.

Following the incident, reports surfaced claiming six people had died in a stampede during the rush to evacuate. However, Divisional Commissioner SM Humayun Kabir Sarkar denied these claims after verifying hospital records and morgue information.
The commissioner stated that one person listed as dead was actually alive, while two others had died of natural causes and were brought to the hospital already dead.
While no one died in a stampede, several people were injured as they rushed downstairs in panic. The Fire Service also confirmed that there were no stampede-related fatalities.
Preliminary suspicions suggest the fire may have started from an electrical short circuit in a non-operational lift, though a full investigation is underway to determine the exact cause.
caption:
Reports of 6 deaths in a stampede at Mymensingh Medical College Hospital have been debunked by the divisional commissioner.

A fire broke out at Mymensingh Medical College Hospital (MMCH) around 6:00 pm on Monday, causing smoke to spread across multiple floors and triggering widespread panic among patients and attendants.

Following the incident, reports surfaced claiming six people had died in a stampede during the rush to evacuate. However, Divisional Commissioner SM Humayun Kabir Sarkar denied these claims after verifying hospital records and morgue information.

The commissioner stated that one person listed as dead was actually alive, while two others had died of natural causes and were brought to the hospital already dead.

While no one died in a stampede, several people were injured as they rushed downstairs in panic. The Fire Service also confirmed that there were no stampede-related fatalities.

Preliminary suspicions suggest the fire may have started from an electrical short circuit in a non-operational lift, though a full investigation is underway to determine the exact cause.
